note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 59; docs/CURRICULUM.md, experiment 3) on data/benches/separate.json: copper oxide separated from copper sulfate by dissolving and filtering, and weighed.
title: Experiment: separating a mixture

steps.title: Your guess
steps.text: The beaker holds 2.000 g of blue copper sulfate crystals and some black copper oxide. How many grams of the oxide do you think there are? Type your guess, then click "predict".
steps.why: A separation works on a difference: here, that copper sulfate dissolves in water and copper oxide does not.

steps.title: Water, stirred
steps.text: Pick up the water and right-click the mixture's beaker; type 40 and click "pour". Right-click the beaker and click "stir".
steps.why: 40 mL of water holds the 2 g of crystals many times over; stirred, they dissolve in a few minutes.

steps.title: Until the crystals are gone
steps.text: Watch the blue spread through the water while the black powder swirls in it.

steps.title: The funnel on the flask
steps.text: Pick up the filter funnel and click the flask: it stands in its neck.
steps.why: The paper's pores are about 11 um across: the solution runs through them, the powder's grains are caught.

steps.title: Pour it through
steps.text: Pick up the stirred mixture and right-click the funnel; type 40 and click "pour": the stirring keeps the powder up, and much of it goes with the liquid.

steps.title: The rest of the powder
steps.text: Pick up the beaker again and right-click the funnel; click "tip in the solid": scrape and rinse what is left in the beaker onto the paper.
steps.why: Every grain left behind is missing from what you weigh: a quantitative transfer leaves none.

steps.title: Until it has drained
steps.text: Wait while the blue filtrate drips into the flask.

steps.title: The dish on the balance
steps.text: Pick up the weighing dish and click the balance; right-click the balance and click "tare".

checks.text: the dish on the balance, tared

steps.title: The powder into the dish
steps.text: Pick up the funnel and right-click the dish; click "tip in the solid": scrape the powder off the paper.

steps.title: Its mass
steps.text: Right-click the balance and click "+ mass".

report.label: the copper oxide in the mixture
report.why: The balance's reading of the dish, tared: every grain transferred, none through the paper. A real residue is weighed dried: a paper and its powder hold water until an oven drives it off.
